full_judgment: 2. The short fact is that the suit property in Dag Nos.701, 700, 973 and 400 corresponding to Khatian Nos.127, 222, 307, 308, 309, 310 and 311 under Mouza-Moillakanda, Thana-Gouripur, District-Mymensingh belonged to defendant No.1, Krishan Lal Agarwala. The defendant No.1 entered into an agreement for sale of the said land on 05.07.1970 with the plaintiff at a consideration of Tk. 75 000/- out of which Tk. 50,000/was paid by him as earnest money. It was stipulated that the sale deed would be executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff within 3(three) years after receiving income-tax clearance certificate as well as the payment of balance consideration, failing which the plaintiff would be at liberty to get a sale deed executed and registered through court. The plaintiff at the material time was ready and willing to pay the balance consideration money to the defendant No.1 but he avoided receiving the same. The plaintiffs wife had a joint business transaction with the defendant No.1. It was assured by the defendant No.1 that the joint business would continue till the sale deed was executed and registered. Thereafter, the plaintiff paid Tk.20, 000/-out of the balance consideration money on 3.3.1971 and obtained a receipt, Thereafter the liberation war was started and the defendant No.1 left for India. During the liberation movement the suit property along with the structures upon it such as godown, offices etc. were completely gutted into ashes by fire. The plaintiff expected that the saf-kabala deed would be executed and registered soon after the liberation. After the liberation war the defendant No.2, Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Vested and Abandoned Property), Mymensingh claiming the suit property to be enemy property leased out the same in favour of the defendant Nos.4-10. Soon after the liberation the plaintiff on several occasions communicated with the defendant No.1 insisting him to execute the kabala. In reply the defendant No.1 repeatedly assured that he would return to Bangladesh and complete the execution in no time. While the plaintiff was ahead of defendant No.1, the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh (defendant No.2) Additional Deputy Commissioner (vested and abandoned property) Mymensingh (defendant No.3) and Chairman, Board of Administration of the Vested Property, Dhaka (defendant No.4) made an attempt to sell out the suit land.
